issues.failure_explanation: The valid intermediate bound has coefficient (\ve/h_i)\sigma(\bar\rho_i)=\alpha/(1-e^{-\bar\rho_i}) on D^-Z. Replacing it by \alpha/(1-e^{-\bar\rho_{i+1}}) requires \bar\rho_i\le\bar\rho_{i+1}, i.e. h_i\le h_{i+1}. On this mesh h_i\ge h_{i+1}, with strict inequality at x_i=1-\tau_x. Counterexample: take Z=\min(x,1-\tau_x), so D^-Z=1 and D^+Z=0 at the transition. Then L^NZ=\ve\sigma(\rho_i)/\bar h_i\approx 2\bar a=O(1), while the stated right side is \approx\alpha/\bar\rho_{i+1}=\alpha N/(4\ln N). The corollary therefore fails for large N.

issues.failure_explanation: By the paper's own bound (trunc-error-sharp), the truncation error contains Ch\min\{1,h/\ve\}\ve|\partial_x\partial_y^2 u|. In the coarse x-region (H\sim N^{-1}\gg\ve) this is CH\ve|\partial_x\partial_y^2 w_N|. Since Lw_N=0, \ve\partial_x\partial_y^2w_N=(a\partial_xw_N)_x-\ve\partial_x^3w_N, and only |\partial_x^2w_N|\le Ce^{-(1-y)/\sqrt\ve} is available. So the term is O(N^{-1})e^{-(1-y)/\sqrt\ve} throughout (0,1-\tau_x)\times(1-\tau_y,1). This reflects the lumped y-diffusion at node x_i with no right-hand-side compensation for Lw=0. The claimed bound h^2/\ve\cdot e^{-\alpha(1-x)/\ve} has no basis for w_N. The stated barrier, whose exponential term is negligible there, cannot dominate an O(N^{-1}) source. Its CN^{-1}B_3 term even contributes an O(N^{-1}) error.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must show that the O(H)(a\partial_x w_N)_x truncation component in the coarse x-region produces only an O(N^{-2}) nodal error (e.g., via a new discrete Green's-function or summation argument). Alternatively, the scheme must be modified (e.g., by not lumping the y-diffusion) and the analysis redone.
issues.overall_effect: The second-order (up to logs) bounds for W_N-w_N and W_S-w_S, and hence the higher-order global bound of Theorem 1 and the abstract's higher-order claim, are unsupported in the singularly perturbed (non-uniform mesh) regime. The proof as written yields only first order.
issues.title: First-order truncation error of characteristic layer in coarse x-region is ignored
issues.why_classification: The central higher-order guarantee for the characteristic layers, the paper's main selling point, is not established. No local fix is available, and recovering it needs a new argument or scheme change.
